newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 6.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

After intense pressure from the car industry, the Federal Government has announced it will freeze automotive tariffs at 15 per cent until 2005, when they will be dropped to 10 per cent. The move follows several days of negotiations and has been approved by the chief executives of Ford, General-Motors Holden, Toyota, and Mitsubishi. Page 1.

Australia's image in Asia has been dampened by the Pauline Hanson phenomenon, with Australian-Thai Chamber of Commerce head Gary White, who is also a senior banker, saying senior Thai business leaders have raised questions on Hanson, which does not allow or productive business dealings. Page 1.

In a move reflecting the Federal Government's concerns that the G7 summit meeting and the international environment meeting could further push calls for legally-binding greenhouse gas targets, Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer has written to the leaders taking part in G7 to argue Australia's case for not conforming to the targets. Page 3.

A survey by major recruiting agency Morgan and Banks has found allowing employees to dress casually at work is becoming increasingly popular and lifts productivity. The survey found 42 per cent of Australian companies allowed mufti days, and 8.4 percent allowed them each week. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard was joined by car industry executives yesterday when he announced the Federal Government would accept a four-year freeze on car tariffs from 2000 to 2004. Howard said car tariffs would be frozen at 15 per cent, then drop to 10 er cent in 2005, before another review for 2006 to 2010. Page 1.

Rupert Murdoch's son Lachlan, 25, has been appointed the chairman of News Limited, the company where he already holds the position of managing director. Murdoch will take over from executive chairman Ken Cowley, who has led the company for more than 17 yars. Page 1.

In a victory for the petrol giants, Federal Court judge Justice Heerey has rejected an attempt by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission to have Mobil, BP and Shell found guilty of price-fixing petrol prices in Sydney and Melbourne in 1991, afer finding that talks which occurred between the petrol retailers did not amount to the "language of arrangement making". Page 1.

Following claims in a report by the Productivity Commission that consumers were being charged five times the actual cost of international telephone calls, Communications Minister Richard Alston has struck out at telecommunications carriers Telstra and Opts, saying customers had received a "raw deal" through the lack of competition in the market. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

After a three and a half year inquest into the death of professional hit man Christopher Dale Flannery, former State Coroner Greg Glass found Flannery dead, and suggested he probably has been since his disappearance 12 years ago. There is a strong suspicon that disgraced detective Roger Rogerson was involved in Flannery's disappearance and death. Page 1.

Following meetings between senior ministers over the last few days, the Federal Government has offered a compromise plan on car tariffs to the car industry, which will see tariffs frozen at 15 per cent from 2000 to 2005. Under the plan, the Government wil legislate in 2005 to drop tariffs to 10 per cent. Page 1.

New South Wales' largest licensed clubs have offered to introduce new gambling measures if the State Government agrees to drop the A$74 million tax increase on poker machines. The clubs say the new measures, including super jackpots, casino-style compute gaming, and jackpot prizes of cars and houses, will more than make up the shortfall. Page 1.

In a A$2.2 billion bid that leaves the Foster's Brewing Group Australian controlled and without a big shareholder for the first time since the Elders group took over in 1983, BHP and Japanese company Asahi have sold their shares in the company. The sale is the largest of its kind in Australia and will take up three stages. Page 1.
THE AGE

Prime Minister John Howard announced yesterday the Federal Government will keep tariffs on domestic cars at 15 per cent for five years from 2000, then reduce them to 10 per cent in one hit. The decision was endorsed by the heads of four Australian car maufacturers, who said it would allow car makers to make future investments and avoid job losses. Page 1.

There will be three stages in the A$2.4 billion deal that saw BHP and Japanese brewer Asahi sell out of the Foster's Brewing Group: BHP will sell its 31.4 per cent share of Foster's to brokers for A$1.53 million; Foster's will cancel the A$625 million purhase of 13 per cent of the company by Asahi; and the final 5 per cent of BHP's share to BHP shareholders will take place later this year. Page 1.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett admitted the Government's surprise release of the Intergraph contract was partly designed to avoid Treasurer Alan Stockdale, former Health Minister Marie Tehan, and Deputy Premier Pat McNamara having to face up to the Adminitrative Appeals Tribunal next week. Page A3.

The Victorian ski season begins this weekend, with the Alpine Resorts Commission expecting more resorts to have light snow cover, and the Bureau of Meteorology saying rain was forecast for today, which may turn to snow overnight. Both bodies were uncertan about the outlook for the rest of the season. Page A3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
